  MEMORANDUM

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

FROM:  ANTON DAHLERBRUCH, CITY MANAGER /s/

SUBJECT: CONSIDERATION OF EXTENDING THE NUMBER OF MEETINGS
  AND DATE FOR RECEIVING RECOMMENDATIONS OF
  TECHNOLOGY TASK FORCE AND AFFIRM THE INTENT OF THE
  TASK FORCE

DATE:  OCTOBER 30, 2017

ISSUE/PURPOSE

Shall the City Council extend the number of meetings of the Technology Task Force and the
date for the Task Force’s presentation of recommendations and affirm the intent of the Task
Force?

BACKGROUND

On June 13, 2017, the City Council appointed five residents to the Technology Task Force
for the general purpose of making a recommendation on whether or not the City Council
should establish a Technology Committee and, if so, the purpose and scope of such a
committee. The Task Force was not provided specific direction relative to, for example, if
their recommendations should consider external connectivity to and among residents for
infrastructure planning and anticipating new technologies, or internal City operations such as
operating systems and the development and management of City resources. While the City
Council “received and filed” the staff report (found here), the report simply included the
following statement:

  Designated to meet monthly in 3 times between July and October and report its
  recommendation(s) to the City Council on November 14, 2017

  Page 1 of 3

  005
 In this regard, the posted agenda for the third meeting of the Task Force on October 19, 2017
listed the meeting at 10:00 a.m. However, on the City’s website, the time of 3:30 p.m. was
unintentionally posted, as called to the City’s attention in the attached correspondence. In
addition, after the meeting concluded, one member of the public came to City Hall to attend
the meeting based on the website posting of 3:30 p.m. Incidentally, due to mis-calendaring
the time, the Committee Chairperson also missed the meeting.

At the meeting on October 19, 2017, the Task Force members in attendance developed their
recommendations for the City Council. In the end, the final report was approved by a quorum
of 3 of the 5 Task Force members.

DISCUSSION

Along with the Task Force Chairperson, City staff understands that the focus of the Task
Force is to ascertain if a Technology Committee is recommended for addressing the
application and deployment of current and anticipated technologies for the “external” quality
of life needs and interests of residents. As such, it is for the Task Force to determine if a
Technology Committee would be valuable for visioning, master planning, considering
infrastructure improvements, the impacts and needs for autonomous vehicles, wireless
antenna siting, commercial use of drones, etc. In contrast, the Task Force is not tasked to
assess the need for a Technology Committee relative to the “internal” functionality; how the
city uses technology to interact with the residents; implementation and management of the
City’s internal operating systems; how the City performs and its services through the use of
technology; specific technologies the City should utilize or deploy, the allocation of City
resources, etc. If the City Council intended for the latter to be included within the scope of
the Task Force, this direction is necessary.

Because the intent of the City Council in June 2017 was for the Task Force to have 3 meetings
and present its recommendations on November 14, 2017, it is being requested that the City
Council extend the allowance for meetings and the date for the Task Force presentation. The
value of extending the number of meetings and date of the presentation is to accommodate
the public who are interested in providing input to the Task Force, for having participation at
the meeting by the entire Task Force, and providing for further review of the final document.
Furthermore, it was unknown at the time that the Chairperson of the Task Force is unable to
attend the November 14 meeting.

FISCAL IMPACT

The City Council prescribed that the Task Force meeting during regular business hours. As
such, the cost is in-kind staff time for the hours of the meeting.

NOTIFICATION

This agenda item has been noticed and posted according to the City’s requirements.

ALTERNATIVES

The alternatives available to the City Council include:

  Page 2 of 3

  006
 1. Extend the number of meetings of, and the date for presentation of recommendations by,
  the Task Force. The City Council may want to specify the number of meetings and / or
  date for the presentation.

2. Decline the extension and have the presentation of the Task Force report at the November
  14, 2017 City Council meeting.

3. Affirm the intent of the Task Force as described herein.

4. Modify the scope of Task Force.

5. Request additional information and / or provide alternate direction.

CONCLUSION/RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council extend the number of meetings that the Technology
Task Force can meet and extend the date for the presentation of the Task Force
recommendation(s) and affirm the intent of the Task Force as described herein.

  Technology Task Force Report to
  the City of Palos Verdes Estates City Council
  November 14, 2017

I.  Introduction and General Recommendation
The City Council has asked the Technology Task Force to make a recommendation regarding the
establishment of a technology advisory committee to the city government. The Task Force has made a
unanimous decision that there is a strong and timely need for an independent source of technology
related advice to enable the city government to deal with an extraordinary number of technology issues.
These issues are now, or will soon enough, be affecting the everyday lives of the citizens of Palos Verdes
Estates. This report will detail the major issues of concern and make a recommendation as to the size,
constitution and method of operation of such a committee.
The key area of concern addressed by this report are:
  1)  Dealing with current telecommunication issues facing the city
  2)  Using technology to improve resident engagement with the City
  3)  Using technology to improve government transparency
  4)  Planning for future technologies
  5)  Develop standards for vendors providing technology solutions to the city

II.  Guiding Principles and Proposed Scope
  A. Guiding Principles
  The Technology Committee shall guide their activities according to the following principles:
  ● The Technology Committee exists to serve the residents of PVE and further their interests
  ● The activities of the Technology Committee shall be reported in a way that allows resident
  awareness and seek to enhance resident inputs
  The Technology Committee will monitor and evaluate evolving technologies and study how those
  will impact the city. The committee will evaluate these technologies and recommend actions in
  order to optimally prepare for and leverage based on at least the following criteria:
  •  Anticipation of new technologies in a way to maximize and accelerate the benefits to the
  residents
  •  Enhance city operations transparency and enable the residents to have greater visibility to
  the operation of the city
  •  Improve city efficiency or enable the city to meet goals with lower costs
  •  Optimize adoption of technologies in a way that maintains the city aesthetics
  The Technology Committee may host educational events and workshops to provide residents
  opportunities to learn about current and future technologies, including: 5G wireless, cyber security,
  and other technology-related issues.

  Page 1

  009
 B. Proposed Scope

  1. Address Telecommunications
  A. Cell Tower Siting
  The Palos Verdes Estates Planning Commission’s agenda had no wireless telecommunication
  facility applications for review in 2013, and then had a few in 2014. In 2015, the Planning
  Commission saw a sharp rise in applications. Therefore, it is vitally important that we focus
  the utmost attention to the installations that will occur, as the current proposed expansion
  is a significant increase in the number of wireless antennas throughout the City and will be
  with us for a long time. The Technology Committee is recommended to provide a long-range
  vision to assist the Planning Commission to appropriately site and provide guidance to the
  design of cell towers.
  B. Improve Broadband Internet Access
  As the wireless infrastructure in Palos Verdes Estates is expanded, so too will the fiber optic
  infrastructure that provides transport of the wireless traffic. Currently, the City of Palos
  Verdes Estates does not have a complete inventory of fiber optic and traditional telephone
  lines existing in the City. The Technology Committee could assist the City develop and
  maintain a comprehensive inventory of telecommunications infrastructure in Palos Verdes
  Estates and the creation of a Technology Master Plan.
  2. Improve Resident Engagement with the City
  The Technology Committee should evaluate electronic communications with residents to
  enhance open discussion about resident concerns. Additionally, surveys could be conducted
  to find out resident positions on City responsiveness to resident concerns and governments
  accountability for serving the residents. Further, the Technology Committee may evaluate
  and recommend technologies to improve resident engagement with the City could include
  social media, City website, surveys, video-conferencing technologies, etc.
  3. Improve Government Transparency
  The Technology Committee should provide technical solutions to align government
  transparency with national standards (National Transparency Association). Community trust
  is challenged by the City, having engaged in 7 years of deficit spending, leaving residents
  concerned about where all the money is going; hence, to build trust, government should
  engage in activities that show the City has nothing to hide and is receptive of resident
  concerns. For example, by publishing legally permissible city records to a searchable on-line
  repository, the city would provide greater ease of use by Staff; facilitating efficiency,
  reduce/eliminate fraud and the perception of wrong doing, and leave the city better
  prepared for disaster recovery.

  Page 2

  010
   4. Future Technologies
  The Technology Task Force believes that PVE can best prepare for the evolution of
  technology by tasking a Technology Committee to monitor and advise on a broad range of
  topics. In addition to telecommunications, the everyday lives of the residents will likely be
  influenced by developments both anticipated and surprising. We expect that the committee
  will evaluate, for example, the roll out of 5G wireless networks, and making
  recommendations to preparing the way, fiber optic and Gigabit home internet service
  providers, communications facilities--ways to enhance city to residents real-time
  communications and modernization of our emergency communications approaches. Also,
  near term availability of integrated solar roof tiles can be investigated, allowing the city to
  inform permit seekers to consider more aesthetically desired choices.
  5. Relationship with Providers
  By helping the City to develop standards for dealing with technology related suppliers, the
  Technology Committee can help on two major fronts. First, to protect Resident Privacy and
  Security, the Technology Committee could develop guidelines for standard contractual
  terms and conditions to protect security and privacy of residents’ homes and personal
  information. Second, to implement Quality Accountability into Service Contracts, the
  Technology Committee could develop guidelines for quality requirements into service
  contracts, including implementation of procedures of validation by City Staff to review and
  approve quality metrics are met before invoices are paid.
III.  Method of Operations
  A. Size
  We believe that a Technology Committee should be established with a minimum number of five (5)
  residents of Palos Verdes Estates.
  B. Composition of Committee
  The members of the Technology Committee will need to see beyond just the technology, we
  recommend that members of the Technology Committee consist of a broad range of expertise, and
  envision the establishment of sub-committees made up of additional volunteers with more specific
  technical backgrounds tailored to the specific tasking.
  The Technology Committee may opt to form subcommittees. Members of subcommittees may not
  need to be residents in order to provide a certain level of technical expertise. Preference for
  subcommittee members shall be given to residents.
  C. Frequency of Meetings and Staffing
  We recommend that the Technology Committee meet initially once a month to formulate a business
  rhythm and subsequently recommend the frequency of meetings to the City Council for formal
  adoption through Resolution for future meetings. City staffing would be identified depending on the
  Technology Committee’s scope.
  D. Duration of Terms of Service
  We propose that the members serve 2-year staggered terms and that the Technology Committee is
  a standing committee as determined by the City Council.

  Technology Task Force
  Recommendation to the
  City of Palos Verdes Estates City Council
  (Date)

I.  Introduction and General Recommendation
The City Council formed the Technology Task Force to make a recommendation about whether or not
the City should have a standing Technology Committee, and if so, the scope / purpose of the Committee.
The Task Force has made a unanimous decision that there is a strong and timely need for an
independent committee to provide technology-related advice to enable the City to deal with an
extraordinary number of technology issues. These issues are now, or will soon enough, be affecting the
everyday lives of Palos Verdes Estates residents. This report will detail the purpose and value a
Technology Committee for the City Council and make a recommendation as to the operations of such a
committee.
The key area of concern addressed by this report are:
  1)  Dealing with current telecommunication issues facing the City,
  2)  Using technology to improve resident engagement with the City,
  3)  Using technology to improve government transparency,
  4)  Planning for future technologies, and
  5)  Develop standards for vendors providing technology solutions to the City.

II.  Guiding Principles and Proposed Scope

  A. Guiding Principles
  The Technology Committee shall guide their activities according to the following principles:
  •  The Technology Committee exists to serve the City Council for the delivery of services to
  residents.
  •  The products of the Technology Committee shall be developed in conformance with
  open meeting requirements and through public outreach, inclusive of public input.
  The Technology Committee will monitor and evaluate evolving technologies and study how those
  will impact the City. The Committee will evaluate these technologies and recommend actions in
  order to optimally:
  •  Prepare for new technologies in a way to maximize and accelerate the benefits to the
  residents,
  •  Enhance the City’s operational systems that provide for transparency and enable residents
  to have greater access to City data and information,
  •  Improve City efficiency and enable the City to meet goals with lower costs, and
  •  Optimize adoption of technologies in a way that maintains city aesthetics.
  The Technology Committee may host educational events and workshops to provide residents with
  opportunities to learn about current and future technologies, including: 5G wireless, cyber security,
  and other technology-related issues.

  Page 1 of 4

  012
 B. Proposed Scope

  1. Telecommunications

  A. Cell Tower Siting
  The Planning Commission had no wireless telecommunication facility applications for review
  in 2013 and 2014. In 2015, the Planning Commission received 23 applications. In 2016, the
  Planning Commission received 3 applications and year to date in 2017, the Planning
  Commission has received 11 applications. It is vitally important that the City retains control
  over “time, place, and manner” in the siting process. The Technology Committee is
  recommended to provide a long-range vision to assist the Planning Commission to
  appropriately site and provide guidance to the design of cell towers.

  Since the original draft of the Task Force report was compiled, Governor Jerry Brown vetoed
  SB 649. SB 649 would have substantially restricted the City’s ability to regulate how and
  where cell sites were located in the City, and what fees could be charged for use of public
  property. This bill was sponsored by the telecommunications industry to limit municipal
  involvement and expedite high-speed wireless internet deployment throughout the State. It
  is unlikely that the telecommunications industry will give up on this type of legislation,
  which has been passed in other States. It is also likely that groups of California cities will
  band together to offer competing legislation, that promotes the goal of widespread wireless
  internet connectivity, without the heavy-handed bashing of cities’ interest in the
  deployment of new sites. The Task Force strongly recommends that the City take a strong
  role in the legislation that is detrimental to the City, and through a Technology Committee.

  B. Improve Broadband Internet Access
  As the wireless infrastructure in Palos Verdes Estates is expanded, so too will the fiber optic
  infrastructure that provides transport of the wireless traffic. Currently, the City does not
  have a complete inventory of existing fiber optic and traditional telephone lines. The
  Technology Committee will assist the City develop and maintain a comprehensive inventory
  of telecommunications infrastructure in Palos Verdes Estates and the creation of a
  Technology Master Plan.
  The South Bay Workforce Investment Board, Inc. and the South Bay Cities Council of
  Governments have worked together to develop a Fiber-optic Master Plan that calls for the
  delivery of economical very high capacity internet service to each of the South Bay cities,
  taking advantage of available subsidies. If this plan is successful, it will open opportunities
  for both cost savings to Palos Verdes Estates and the ability for the City to offer internet
  services to its residents in some fashion should that be required. The Technology Task Force
  recommends that the City take an active role in the furthering of this plan.
  2. Resident Engagement with the City
  The Technology Committee should evaluate and develop recommendations for the City’s
  technology systems for communications and connectivity with residents to enhance civic
  engagement inclusive of social media, City website, surveys, video-conferencing

  Page 2 of 4

  013
   technologies, electronic voting, etc. The Technology Committee will use a variety of means
  to receive public input in developing its recommendations.

  3. Government Transparency

  The Technology Committee will recommend technical solutions to align with best practices
  for government transparency. Technology provides a means to connect with residents for
  providing information, civic engagement, and trust. For example, technology can facilitate
  the accessibility to a variety of City information.

  4. Future Technologies
  The Technology Task Force believes that Palos Verdes Estates can best prepare for the
  evolution of technology by tasking a Technology Committee to monitor and advise on a
  broad range of topics. In addition to telecommunications, the everyday lives of the residents
  will likely be influenced by developments both anticipated and surprising. The committee
  will evaluate, for example, the roll out of 5G wireless networks, and making
  recommendations to preparing the way, fiber optic and Gigabit home internet service
  providers, communications facilities--ways to enhance city to residents real-time
  communications and modernization of emergency communications and disaster recovery.
  Also, new technology such as integrated solar roof tiles can be investigated for improving
  the choices for decision makers.
  5. Standards for Vendors
  Through its knowledge, experience and research, the Technology Committee will provide
  recommendations for operational and contractual standards with technology related
  suppliers. The Technology Committee will provide insight and recommendations for
  contracts and implementation of cyber security, backup and recovery of City information
  and electronic data. The Technology Committee will also provide recommendations of
  technology systems for managing the City’s records.

III.  Method of Operations

  A. Size
  A Technology Committee should be established with a minimum of five (5) Palos Verdes Estates
  residents.
  B. Composition of Committee
  The members of the Technology Committee should be visionaries and consist of a broad range of
  expertise.
  As needed, the Technology Committee should not be prohibited from forming subcommittees or ad
  hoc committees, which may include additional volunteers who are not committee members with
  more specific technical backgrounds tailored to specific tasks. Members of subcommittees or ad hoc
  committees may not need to be residents in order to provide a certain level of technical expertise.
  Preference for subcommittee and ad hoc committee members shall be given to residents.
  C. Frequency of Meetings and Staffing

  Page 3 of 4

  014
 The Technology Committee should meet initially once a month to formulate a business rhythm and
subsequently recommend the frequency of meetings to the City Council for formal adoption through
Resolution for future meetings. Appropriate City staff will be assigned pending the scope of the
Technology Committee.
D. Duration of Terms of Service
Members will serve 2-year staggered terms. The Technology Committee is a standing committee as
determined by the City Council.
